reasons: Only one of eight sections was included, so the conversion is not reviewed.
No test is visible for this file.
The packet does not show error handling.

terms.meaning: A styling toolkit that uses short class names built from a configuration file.
Named values in CSS that many styles can reuse.
A file of settings that a program reads at startup.

depends_on: the design token JSON file, such as assets/design-tokens.json
Node.js built-in fs and path modules

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Header, usage, and imports
sections.what: Describes the script's purpose and shows two usage examples: one writing CSS to a file, and one writing Tailwind output. It also imports the file and path tools it needs.
sections.why: Records how the script is meant to be run and provides the tools for reading and writing files.
sections.watch_out: The usage examples show the options but not the expected token file layout, so a wrongly shaped file is not caught by these notes.

sections.name: parseArgs
sections.title: Reads command options
sections.what: Reads the command-line flags for the input token file, the output file, the output format (CSS or Tailwind), and a help option that prints usage and exits.
sections.why: Lets the same script produce either CSS or a Tailwind config from one token file.
sections.watch_out: A flag given without a value, such as a trailing output flag, is read as empty instead of raising an error.

sections.name: resolveReference
sections.title: Follows token links to their final value
sections.what: When a token value points to another token, written inside curly braces, this follows the chain until it reaches a real value. If the target is not found, it returns the original text.
sections.why: Lets one token reuse another so that a change in one place flows through.
sections.watch_out: A token that points back to itself would loop forever, and the code has no guard against this.

sections.name: toCssVarName
sections.title: Converts token names to variable names
sections.what: Joins the parts of a token's path with dashes and adds the double dash prefix that CSS variables need.
sections.why: Gives each token a predictable CSS variable name that matches the design token convention.
sections.watch_out: Two different token paths could join to the same name, and the later one would silently overwrite the earlier one.

sections.name: flattenTokens
sections.title: Flattens nested tokens into a list
sections.what: Walks through nested groups of tokens and collects each final token with its name and resolved value into one flat list.
sections.why: CSS needs one flat list of variables, not a nested structure.
sections.watch_out: Anything that is not an object with a value is skipped without any message.

sections.name: generateCSS
sections.title: Builds the CSS output
sections.what: Writes three root groups (primitives, semantic, components) and a dark mode group from the flattened tokens. The file header says it should not be edited by hand.
sections.why: Produces the shared stylesheet that every page and component reads.
sections.watch_out: The header tells people to edit a file called tokens.json, but the real input is whichever file is passed with the config flag, so the header may mislead.

sections.name: generateTailwind
sections.title: Builds the Tailwind color output
sections.what: Picks out only the semantic tokens whose names include the word color and turns them into a color map that points to the CSS variables.
sections.why: Lets the Tailwind styling tool use the same brand colors as the CSS.
sections.watch_out: Tokens without the word color in their name, such as spacing or fonts, are not exported to Tailwind.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Main run
sections.what: Reads the options, checks the config file exists, reads and parses the JSON, picks CSS or Tailwind, and writes the result to a file or prints it.
sections.why: Ties all the steps together into one command.
sections.watch_out: A badly formed JSON file stops the script with a raw error message and no friendly explanation.

summary: Converts a design token JSON file into CSS variables, or optionally a Tailwind setup. Only the header and imports were included in this packet, so the conversion steps are not reviewed.
purpose: Turns the shared design token file into a form that web pages and styling tools can read.
why: Likely reason: the token JSON is the single source of design values, and CSS needs variables in its own format.
how: The script reads command options for the config file, the output file, and the output format, then converts the token file. The conversion steps are not in this packet.
inputs: A token JSON config file and command options for the output file and format.
outputs: A CSS variables file, or Tailwind output when that format is chosen. Whether it writes the file directly is not shown in the packet.
risks: Without the conversion code, errors in naming or references cannot be checked here.
debug: If the CSS is stale or missing values, run the script by hand with the config option and check the output file. Also check the token JSON for broken references.
